title: Is It True That I 'Don't Get

sentences: When people say: 'I never get angry,' what they really mean is they just contain it really well – and often at their own expense," says Sam Parker, a senior editor at British GQ and author of Good Anger: How Rethinking Rage Can Change Our Lives.
translations: 当人们说‘我从不生气’时，他们真正的意思只是他们很好地压抑了愤怒——而且常常是以牺牲自己为代价，”英国GQ杂志高级编辑、《好愤怒：重新思考愤怒如何改变我们的生活》一书的作者萨姆·帕克说道。

sentences: He used to believe that "the only people with an anger issue were the people who kept getting into fights and arguments, and losing their temper," Parker tells me.
"I had this idea that I was somehow beyond anger, or it was just of no use to me."
translations: 帕克告诉我，他曾经认为“只有那些不断打架、争吵、发脾气的人才有愤怒问题。”
“我曾以为自己在某种程度上超越了愤怒，或者愤怒对我毫无用处。”

sentences: He did struggle with anxiety.
And when he hit a rough patch in his 30s, Parker tried yoga, meditation, gratitude journaling and even cold showers.
What worked?
Boxing.
translations: 他确实与焦虑作斗争。
当他在三十多岁时遇到困难时期，帕克尝试了瑜伽、冥想、感恩日记甚至冷水澡。
什么有效呢？
拳击。

sentences: A couple of months in, while letting loose on the bag, Parker was unexpectedly overcome by emotion, enough to wet his eyes.
"For the first time in months I wasn't sad or anxious," he writes.
"I was furious."
translations: 几个月后，当帕克在沙袋上尽情发泄时，他意外地被情绪淹没，泪水盈眶。
"几个月来第一次，我不再悲伤或焦虑，"他写道。
"我愤怒至极。"

sentences: Over time, it dawned on him: "The more that I recognised anger in myself, talked about it, processed it and eventually acted on it, the more my anxiety went down."
translations: 随着时间的推移，他逐渐意识到：“我越是认识到自己内心的愤怒，谈论它，处理它，并最终采取行动，我的焦虑就越少。”

sentences: After that epiphany, Parker learned there was a well-established scientific link between anger and anxiety – it just wasn't widely acknowledged.
translations: 在那次顿悟之后，帕克了解到愤怒与焦虑之间存在着公认的科学联系——只是这种联系并未得到广泛认可。

sentences: To him, it represented a critical oversight in the mental-health conversation.
Anger is as natural as sadness, fear, happiness or disgust – but it's often left out of the picture.
translations: 对他来说，这代表了心理健康讨论中的一个关键疏忽。
愤怒与悲伤、恐惧、快乐或厌恶一样自然——但它常常被排除在画面之外。

sentences: In part, it's a language problem, Parker explains.
"In English, we conflate 'anger' with 'aggression' or even 'violence', as though they are the same thing."
translations: 帕克解释说，这在一定程度上是一个语言问题。
"在英语中，我们将'愤怒'与'攻击性'甚至'暴力'混为一谈，仿佛它们是同一回事。"

sentences: But it is an especially challenging emotion to experience and be around.
translations: 但这是一种特别难以体验和相处的情绪。

sentences: Whether in pop science or academic research, "across the spectrum, anger is sort of neglected," he says.
translations: 无论是在科普还是学术研究中，“从整体来看，愤怒在某种程度上被忽视了，”他说。

sentences: Parker wrote Good Anger hoping to reframe the emotion, and help others understand, experience and express it differently.
Anger is persistently seen as negative: "We tend to avoid talking about it altogether until it has boiled over into aggression," he says.
This can compound the shame and stigma.
translations: 帕克撰写《好愤怒》一书，希望重新定义这种情绪，并帮助他人以不同的方式理解、体验和表达它。
愤怒一直被视为负面情绪：他说：“我们往往完全避免谈论它，直到它爆发为攻击性行为。”
这可能会加剧羞耻感和污名化。

sentences: "A lot of the time, aggressive behaviour is a choice we make," says Parker.
But the emotion itself is legitimate, exists to protect us – and often has something insightful to say.
translations: "很多时候，攻击性行为是我们做出的选择，"帕克说。
但这种情绪本身是合理的，它存在是为了保护我们——而且常常有深刻的见解要表达。

sentences: "We tend to think that anger's telling us something about other people: how unreasonable they are, how they're out to get us, why they're idiots … Far more often, it's pointing us towards an unmet need or event from the past," he says.
translations: “我们倾向于认为愤怒在告诉我们关于他人的一些事情：他们多么不讲道理，他们如何针对我们，为什么他们是白痴……但更多时候，它指向的是我们未满足的需求或过去的某件事，”他说。

sentences: When proportionately experienced, anger is not only part of a balanced emotional mix – it can also be "a real source of determination, vitality and clarity", Parker says, pointing us towards what we value and spurring us on.
translations: 当适度体验时，愤怒不仅是平衡情感组合的一部分——它还可以成为“决心、活力和清晰度的真正源泉”，帕克说，它指引我们珍视的事物并激励我们前进。

sentences: When he finally acknowledged and began attuning to his latent anger, "that was when I started to see the real benefits."
translations: 当他终于承认并开始适应自己潜藏的愤怒时，"那是我开始看到真正益处的时候。"

sentences: Parker's right: it's not really accurate for me to say "I never get angry."
I just avoid acknowledging it, or name it something more palatable, such as irritation or disappointment.
translations: 帕克说得对：我说“我从不生气”其实并不准确。
我只是避免承认它，或者给它起个更悦耳的名字，比如烦躁或失望。

sentences: I associate this aversion with my adolescence, when I frequently gave into anger, lashing out at my family and feeling unpleasantly out of control.
translations: 我将这种厌恶与我的青春期联系起来，那时我经常屈服于愤怒，对家人大发雷霆，并感到一种令人不快的失控感。

sentences: "Trait anger" is inherent and individual, influenced by genetics and environment.
Having high trait anger means you're quicker than others to fly off the handle.
"State anger", on the other hand, is temporary, triggered by frustration or a perceived threat.
translations: "特质愤怒"是与生俱来且因人而异的，受遗传和环境的影响。
特质愤怒程度高意味着你比他人更容易发火。
而"状态愤怒"则是暂时的，由挫折或感知到的威胁所引发。

sentences: "No one gets away without having state anger," says Parker.
The question is, how do you typically express it?
Anger researchers distinguish between "anger-out" and "anger-in": externalising the emotion through physical or verbal aggression, versus striving to contain it and, in doing so, turning it inwards.
translations: "没有人能逃脱愤怒的状态，"帕克说。
问题是，你通常如何表达它？
愤怒研究者区分了"外显愤怒"和"内隐愤怒"：通过身体或言语攻击将情绪外化，与努力抑制它并在此过程中将其转向内在。

sentences: The former might be more familiar (and harder to ignore), but the "anger-in" crowd are suffering in silence, Parker says.
Such containment is unsustainable and can carry a high personal cost: "Anger deferred is anger multiplied."
translations: 前者可能更为常见（也更难忽视），但帕克表示，那些“压抑愤怒”的人正在默默承受痛苦。
这种压抑是不可持续的，并且可能带来高昂的个人代价：“被推迟的愤怒会成倍增长。”

sentences: Refusing to acknowledge anger may even make people sick, Parker says, pointing to the deleterious effects of sustained elevated cortisol, the stress hormone.
translations: 帕克指出，拒绝承认愤怒甚至可能让人生病，并提到了持续升高的压力荷尔蒙皮质醇的有害影响。

sentences: A healthy relationship with anger entails active, open engagement – neither denying its existence nor letting it run the show.
translations: 与愤怒建立健康的关系需要积极、开放的参与——既不否认它的存在，也不让它主导一切。

sentences: A better goal is "creating a positive, productive association in your body and mind".
That can be achieved through physical movement, as Parker discovered with boxing; other examples are jogging and dancing.
Anger can also be channelled creatively through journaling, painting or drawing.
translations: 一个更好的目标是“在身心上建立积极、富有成效的联系”。
这可以通过身体运动来实现，正如帕克在拳击中发现的；其他例子包括慢跑和跳舞。
愤怒也可以通过写日记、绘画或素描等创造性方式得到疏导。

sentences: Once past the heat of the moment, you can decide with clarity what, if any, action is necessary, Parker says.
"Sometimes you do have to go and have the scary conversation, and say the difficult thing."
translations: 帕克说，一旦过了情绪激动的时刻，你就能清晰地决定需要采取什么行动（如果有的话）。
“有时候你确实必须去进行那些令人害怕的对话，说出那些难以启齿的事情。”

sentences: Other times, merely acknowledging how you feel is enough to lessen the sting, and help you move on.
translations: 其他时候，仅仅承认自己的感受就足以减轻痛苦，并帮助你继续前行。
